newsitem.title: MONGOLIA: Mongolia expels North Korea diplomat for fake cash.
newsitem.headline: Mongolia expels North Korea diplomat for fake cash.

text.p: Mongolia has ordered a North Korean diplomat to leave the country after he was arrested for passing fake U.S. dollar bills to black market moneychangers, police officials said on Monday.

The diplomat, a third secretary at the North Korean embassy in Ulan Bator whose name was given as Kim Che-ming, had been told to leave the north Asian nation by December 31, the officials said. It was not clear if he had already left.
South Korean and U.S. media have repeatedly accused Pyongyang of secretly printing dollars, a charge the reclusive Stalinist state has denied.

Mongolian police officials said Kim had swapped $100,000 for tugriks on the Ulan Bator currency black market, but Mongolian moneychangers later discovered they had been left with fake bills and reported him.
The diplomat was arrested when he returned to the black market with a further $19,000 earlier this month, they said.
Authorities in Thailand said last April they would try a former Japanese urban guerrilla travelling with North Korean papers on charges of distributing counterfeit dollars.

Former Red Army guerrilla Yoshimi Tanaka was arrested in Cambodia in March and sent to Thailand to face counterfeiting charges. Two other people detained with him were released after they produced genuine North Korean diplomatic passports.
